artifact: level 0 vs level 1 — project-owned quality comparison
how: the generation evaluation layer, one process per level, run on the OrangePi against the live graph; /tmp/baseline_level{0,1}.json
why: the project had no comparable quality baseline: the gate measured 35 answers and the standalone RAGAS run measured 67 over a different dataset. This compares two detail levels on the gate's own dataset, with the deterministic evidence-usage signal added the same day.
verdict: No clear winner. Level 0 wins the project's own faithfulness (0.879 vs 0.795) and the pairwise judge (0.714 vs 0.400) at a sixth of the latency; level 1 wins RAGAS faithfulness (0.674 vs 0.593) and the deterministic evidence-usage signal; context precision is a tie. The two levels are complementary slices, not one degraded mode.
caveats: evidence_usage (term_grounding) measures vocabulary overlap with the contexts, so it structurally favours the level that sends more context: level 1 sends 164 summaries and level 0 sends 4. It must not be the sole arbiter.
ragas_answer_relevancy is broken in this configuration (a deterministic 0.0 even when the answer is the question echoed back); its values here must not be tuned against.

cited_context_share is null for both levels because the evaluation's contexts carry no citable id (chunk_id is None for community summaries), which is why the signal reports an undefined share instead of a zero.
level 0 carries ragas_drop_warning: true: its RAGAS faithfulness fell below the previous value (0.6825) recorded in the baseline.
